thesis: This episode argues that traditional value stocks like AutoZone and IBM face significant disruption risks from technological shifts, such as driverless vehicles, which could render their current business models obsolete. The speaker suggests that while these companies may appear attractive in systematic value screens, their long-term viability is questionable due to an inability to innovate out of their current cycles.

claims.claim: The speaker believes AutoZone is facing massive disruption risk because fixing cars will become obsolete as driverless Teslas replace traditional vehicles.
claims.quote: One of my favorite shorts right now is AutoZone. And for a lot of different reasons. But like, I would, I can't, I can't, I can't buy any individual names, but I would be buying leaps on this thing because this thing's a zero.

claims.claim: The speaker predicts AutoZone will eventually be dead because driverless Teslas will be fixed by others, making the current business model unsustainable.
claims.quote: Not only that, but in like, you know, five or ten years, you're not going to be driving a car. You're going to be, you know, rolling around in one of these driverless things that Tesla licenses out to you. And they're going to be fixing it because how do you fix a Tesla? Like, good, good luck figuring that out. So, like, AutoZone's dead eventually.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that AutoZone is a classic example of a value stock that screens well in systematic strategies but questions how to price the disruption risk.
claims.quote: The AutoZone's a funny one because it's, it's actually one of the classic examples of a name that screens incredibly well in a lot of systematic strategies, especially those that look at value, at capital allocation, share repurchases, all these things.

claims.claim: The speaker states that a best decile portfolio of value stocks would include AutoZone, highlighting the concern regarding retail and disruption risk.
claims.quote: Because value, if you look at a, if you go look at a best desile portfolio of value stocks, you're going to see retail, you're going to see AutoZone, you're going to see some of these, a lot of these stocks and industries, where your concern is most manifest.

claims.claim: The speaker believes IBM cannot innovate out of its current cycle and suggests it would be a classic value stock that is struggling.
claims.quote: Look at IBM, like, good luck getting IBM to, like, innovate out of this cycle. I just don't see it happening. And that would be a classic value stock right now.
